newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian experts to examine weeds in wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: Indian experts to examine weeds in wheat imports.

text.p: India has set up a group of experts to examine which weed species Australia could be made to declare if they are contained in wheat shipments, a government minister said on Monday.
Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra told reporters Australian authorities had also agreed to provide data to help Indian scientists evolve criteria on tolerance limits of weeds in imported wheat.

"Based upon the recommendations of the expert group, government may also consider appropriate amendments in the PFS (Plants, Fruits and Seeds (Regulations of import into India), Order, 1989," he said.
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has set up the expert group, he said.

A senior Food Ministry official said earlier this month India had decided to go ahead with the purchase of one million tonnes of wheat from Australia, which was stalled due to the presence of weeds in earlier shipments.
India has already bought more than one million tonnes of wheat from Australia since December last year.
Mishra said in June weeds were detected in earlier wheat shipments from Australia but they were not found to be harmful and were common in wheat of any origin.
To ensure that weed seeds did not get established in wheat growing areas, use of imported wheat was restricted only to non-wheat growing areas, Mishra said on Monday.
